**Short answer: not yet.** I would run Opus 6 as one new configuration in round 7 first. Production stays on Q, pinned to its dated `claude-sonnet-5-5` id, until the eval shows a result.

**What I do next**

1. I look up the dated Opus 6 model id and its per-token price in the current Claude API docs. I pin that exact id. I do not use an alias.
2. I draft the round 7 plan below for you to approve in plan mode. I do not touch production, and I do not touch `spe/predictions/r06-draft.yaml`.

**Round 7 plan (draft)**

*Specify*

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R7-1 | Test Opus 6 on the same 60 invoices with the same graders. | User: "Opus 6 is out, should we just move to it?" | Every config is scored on all 60 cells. |
| R7-2 | Keep Q on `claude-sonnet-5-5` as the reference config. | Decision: Q was best at r06. | Q is regraded and its control matches r06. |
| R7-3 | The new config, Q-O6, changes only the model id. | Rule: change one thing per config. | A diff of the config files shows only the model line. |
| R7-4 | Measure field accuracy, cost, time, tokens, tool calls, and tool errors for each invoice. | Way: compare accuracy, cost, tokens, and time. | The trial result schema has all six fields. |
| R7-5 | Do not switch production during the eval. | Way: no production switch before the eval. | No deploy step appears in the Workflow. |

I would carry forward last round's proposals as they appear in `failures.md`. I would adopt or reject each one with a reason once I read it.

*Predict* (Q starts from "same as last round". The bands come from `r06-draft.yaml`.)

| Metric | Q (Sonnet 5.5) | Q-O6 (Opus 6) | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy | 0.93 ± r06 band | 0.95 ± 0.03 | A larger model usually reads messy line items better. The 60 invoices leave little room above 0.93. | Field match against the AP lead's references |
| Cost per invoice | $0.011 ± r06 band | $0.020 ± 0.008 | Opus costs more per token. I will fix this number from the doc price before approval. | Token counts times the list price |
| Seconds per invoice | 14 ± r06 band | 18 ± 5 | Larger models usually respond more slowly. | Wall clock for each trial |
| Tokens, tool calls, tool errors | r06 values | Within 15% of Q | The prompt and tools are the same. | Counts from the transcripts |

I will also write the decision rule down now, before any result exists. Opus 6 is worth switching to only if its accuracy beats Q's band. You then decide whether the extra cost is acceptable. That choice belongs to you.

*Evaluate*

- I copy the r06 harness to `spe/evals/harness/r07-workflow.js`. It uses one `ROUND = 7` constant. It runs two configs on 60 invoices, which is 120 cells, plus top-up trials for cells that passed only some of the time.
- The gates run in order. First the grader selftest runs, where the oracle passes and the empty and wrong answers fail. Next r06 is regraded as a control. Then a dry run on 2 or 3 cells uses `args.only`.
- The arguments set caps on API spend and agent count. Trials may read only the invoice PDFs and the PO data. Any trial that reads `spe/evals/` or `spe/predictions/` is voided.
- My cost estimate is unmeasured. It is about $2 to $4 of model spend for the trials, plus the cost of the judge and synthesis agents.

**After you approve**

1. I save the plan to `spe/plans/r07.md` and write `spe/predictions/r07.yaml`. I commit both locally as one SPE step.
2. I run the gates and then launch the Workflow. When it finishes, I commit the results locally.
3. I report Q-O6 against Q and give a recommendation. I do not push, and I do not change production.
